title: Christmas Day sermons urge unity in ‘common humanity’ to combat divisions in society
summary: Incoming archbishop of Canterbury calls for people to ‘make room’ as Pope Leo decries conditions for Palestinians in Gaza The incoming archbishop of Canterbury has warned in her Christmas Day sermon that “our national conversations about immigration continue to divide us, when our common humanity should unite us”. Acting in her current role as the bishop of London, Dame Sarah Mullally told St Paul’s Cathedral: “Joy is born exactly where despair expects to triumph. As joy breaks through in our lives it gives us the opportunity to become people who make room. Continue reading...
